Overall tour was good. Wasn’t thrilled with the tour guide completely as I felt like we were being rushed through but she did give a lot of history along the way. Would like to have spent more time in the colosseum for photos.

Luis Kennedy was our tour guide. She was do knowledgeable about the coliseum and the history behind everything. She spoke very good English, she was very easy to understand. She was spunky and quite funny. She gave us plenty of time to take pictures. We had such a great time. We would highly recommend her and this tour.

Fantastic tour, our guide Simone was lovely very funny. Took his time to tell you everything. Well worth the money especially the que jump ticket. Only down side was it was difficult to locate our guide as directions not that clear.

This was an average tour, nothing exciting or that I would recommend. Our guide was nice but sadly he was not a very interesting story teller. He also had a strong accent which made it difficult to understand him. My kids lost interest fast and the ear buds were super uncomfortable to wear.

Absolutely excellent experience. Definitely well worth it. Our guide Eddy was superb. He was extremely knowledgeable and entertaining as well. He has an archeology background and a definite passion for the topic. I would highly recommend him as a guide.

Amazing guided tour, with an exceptional guide (Gil) who took all the time to provide us with all the details. She also gave us the opportunity to take all the pictures we wanted. She really knows her stuff! A great experience!

Maria was a wonderful guide. She had great energy and knowledge as she showed us the Colosseum! She knew many awesome facts that were so interesting and new to us. Would certainly come back to tour with her again. She gave us recommendations for sites around the area of Rome as well which was nice of her :)

Rossella was a wonderful guide. Creating a relaxing yet very informative tour. She was incredibly knowledgeable and fun. She provided time for comfort breaks and trips to the gift shop if required.
5 star
My only grumble would be difficulty in finding the meeting point as personally couldn’t find clear information on the ticket. However this a is trip advisor problem not the guides.

Sylvia did an amazing job taking us around the colosseum, palatine hill and the forum. Her passion as an archeologist showed in her excitement for the tour and her knowledge. She did a great job taking us to the most important parts and teaching us amazing facts. He was also very patient with the heat and made sure we never stood in the sun unnecessarily.

Selenia Morgillo excellent guide. Friendly and very detailed with her explanations. Very professional and bring us to her special spots for best view and photo taking. She does gives you time to take some photos. End of the trips gives us some tips where are the best spot to continue our visits. Overall, very friendly lady and funny also.

Silvia was an engaging, brilliant and knowledgeable guide. Sharing many detailed stories to bring the Colosseum, Roman forum and Palatine Hill. There was no question that she could not answer. She also made the visit fun.

Great tour! We enjoyed learning about the history. It is very hot and very little shade, but it was worth it to see all this beauty. Alessandro was our tour guide and he explained everything with great detail. It really helped us understand the history of these monuments. Amazing tour, highly recommend.

In Rome for a day and thought you could by a ticket on site. You can't. They have to be purchased online and we'll ahead of time. I was also approached outside by at least 3 different street vendors pushing friendship bands and various other items. They came across in quite an intimidating fashion.

AMAZING. An extraordinary landscape and buildings to check off the bucket list. Our guide was fabulous: informative, engaging and just all around awesome. Definitely worth it for skipping the queues also! Took everything at a steady pace so it didn’t feel rushed - ❤️❤️❤️

Gabby was a great guide! So much information and she made it all come together for us. She has an easy pace that allows you to take photos, take in what your seeing and still keep moving steady through the 3 areas. Thanks Gabby!

They cancelled the Small Group tour and left us on our own with no help. I continued to get emails as if it was still on. Essentially, no notice. By the way, communication with someone from another country with limited WiFi, text, phone calls is not my problem. They had no trouble telling me how was the tour?

Maria was a Fantastic Guide. Very informative and she made the history come to life. Also we didn’t have to join the long queues so its definitely worth doing booking a skip the line tour. Highly recommended,

The Forum and Colosseum closed early for an Easter celebration. It was only announced a few days prior and obviously the tour group has no control over that, but we were not informed of that until we arrived. We would have liked to have been given the option to reschedule as we didn’t get to see all of the forum. Our tour guide was great though. He tried to get in as much as possible while we could.

We had a great tour today with our tour guide pj. We didn’t have to wait around to get in was all very organised. It’s very admiring and you can clearly see that he is extremely passionate about Rome and it’s history. Definitely would recommend this tour and would also book future tours with city wonders.

100% recommended this tour to anyone who is wanting to see the Colosseum and the tourist parts of Rome.
Nick our tour guide was outstanding. From his knowledge to the small things like water breaks etc.
Nick thank you for making our last day in Rome memorable.

Great tour with Ahmed! He was very knowledgeable, having a lot of fun facts to share. The tour would not have been the same without a guide. The only con was The meeting point was a bit confusing but thankfully we made it on time. I would definitely recommend this tour!

Paola was the most informative, friendly and humorous guide! She is an archeologist and truly loves the topic. We had so much fun and learned so much from her. I give Paola and City Winders my highest recommendation!

Great tour. We loved our guide Guissepe. He was really knowledgable and funny and kind. I was a history major in college and I learned so much from him! The tour was well organized and well paced. We were lucky there were almost no crowds anywhere (due to covid) so it was easy to see everything. Highly recommend.

Our tour guide was very nice, spoke good English and open to answering questions. We learned so much on the tour. I wish we could have been in the Colosseum a little longer. Exploring Palatine Hill was a highlight of the day. I would bring medium to large side backpack if you want to buy souvenirs and carry a traditional camera. Athletic shoes a must.

Loved this guided tour, i would highly recommend. The guide was fantastic and very knowledgable. Lots of stops for photos and always very happy to answer questions. The cafe at the meeting point was very nice also.

Giuseppe was an amazing guide, he knew everything!!!!!!! He is a fantastic historian and really brought the stories of the Romans and gladiators to life. He answered every question we had and made sure we have the best experience. The tour was prompt, on time and easy to follow, there were only 8 of us too which was fab. Would highly recommend!

We took the tour with guide Nick. Very thorough, detailed, and clear experience. He seemed genuinely interested and passionate about the history. Nick answered all our questions well and we learned a lot. He was incredibly nice. Great tour.

This tour is amazing, and the Underground tour is highly recommended and spectacular. Having a good guide makes the experience even better, and our group had an exceptional guide, Makala. She is an expert in the history and tradition of Roman life and architecture, and was especially friendly. She is awesome. Our group of 7 learned, laughed, and had the best time ever! -- Tim F. 8/30/2021

Thank you so much for this wonderful 5 star experience

We recently took the tour of the colleseum, palatine Hill and roman forum and it was excellent. Great value for money. Nicola (spelling?) was our guide and she was very knowledgeable and accommodating throughout the tour. This made the day even better for us.

Very good tour guide. Very tiring. He should have made it more clearly about the very, very steep steps to get up to the colosseum as I am 70. Not to be missed.

Very nice tour guide Laura, easy to understand and a wealth of knowledge. We will not remember all she explained, but gave us a great understanding of the areas we toured. Again a bit over the top with info and the tour could have been more condensed and have the same understanding.

Guide was extremely passionate and knowledgeable. Great understanding of English made his explanations really clear and in-depth. Relaxed and easy going. Only issue was we thought it included the actual floor of the arena and it didn't.

The tour was very knowledgeable and out guide was a wealth of information! It was SO hot and there were various places we had to stay in the sun too long. I understand this was not the guides fault, but be prepared to be in the sun a lot.

Another amazing guide, Elizabeth! Plenty of walking and climbing awkwardly high steps and inclines. Our guide was a retired architect which added a special touch to our tour. Great tour. The guide was very good. Great price!! We could have spent a little more time in the Forum. The red marble on the floor in the picture was very rare in Roman times. Today no more exists.

First question the people ask do I need a guide in Colosseum or Flavian Amphitheatre, the simple answer is Yes, City Wonders was chosen as reputable company, that I did Florence tours, they're one of the best in business and contracting the best telnet. Why do I need a guide the answer is simple - instead of staring on bunch of stones only knowledgeable guides can lead You through details and hidden facts also make the day fun and not boring, especially if they speak English well. The second if not first thing is skip the line, seems like a big deal cause we cruse through the crowded general lines straight to the attractions, I have a feeling it’s like a mafia style everybody gets the cut, but it’s a business so if You want to skip the lines You have to pay.

The way this business operates is that most of the guides are freelancers and Company hires the best telnet so far that I experienced, so it might be little more expensive than the rest of the crowd, but really worth it.

But back to the tour. We came to the tour after Vatican/St Peters half day tour, as a part of a whole days in Rome tour with City Wonders. I'll do a description of the first tour separately, but want to give couple of tips for people who coming from the first tour. The time difference between the tours is 3 hours, You might think it's too much but, not really at all if You look from couple of things.

1. You'll be soaking wet from the first tour in Vatican, since it's the most busiest places and people packed like sardines in hot rooms of the museums. So if you live close by the Vatican like we did, take a quick break, change, take a shower if You can. Then You have two options to walk to Colosseum, which takes approximately 45 minutes (depending on Your age) also consider the heat that would be at 12 PM.
We took the metro from Vatican, which closest station on A branch Ottavia station to Termini, then change to B branch Colosseum usually ride takes 15-20 minutes. We decided to have lunch next to Colosseum instead of Vatican to be on time and by the time we're done it was already 2.45 PM, so 3 hour break between the tours is there for a reason.

Do not miss the meeting point, it’s on the upper exit of the station, not on the bottom, if You exit on the bottom go to the left facing Colosseum, and take stairs on the top.
You probably already annoyed by the folks who tries to sell You staff, but this point, You’ll be flooded with folks trying to sell You battery chargers for the phone, souvenirs, hats, waters and so on.

So good advise do not buy anything from them, once You buy, the rest of the folks will storm You, given this as advise, make sure, You came on tour prepared, wearing HATS, because You’ll spend 60% of the tour under the sun, You own water bottles, which can be re-filled along the way from Roman fountains, that guide will show You (stay hydrated all the time), sun screen is a MUST, if You do not want to get burned, we took the tour in 8 of June 2019, so it was 33C, or 92F.

Ok, now back to the tour, once arrived at meeting point, You have to registered first. Ask any folks with CityWonders flags where to register, to Your surprise it’ll be probably and long line with folks waiting to register, but it goes really quick, the tour guide, I’m not sure if You have options which tour guide to choose from, but if You can choose Valerio – the Architect, since there’s several Valerio’s on the tour, You WILL NOT REGRET.

What would be the best tour guide that You can get?
This is my personal opinion, but here’s the list:
1. Speak English well (sometimes You can understand what the talk is about, but sometimes You hardly can, and this is what You want to avoid). Valerio was born in Rome, then lived in New Your some time, so he has perfect American English.
2. Guide MUST be funny (You probably know what I mean, some guides are just monotone script readers), You can imagine Italian guide that lived in New York, Valerio was funny with a good sense of humor, not over the board, just where it needed.
3. Guide must know the history, obviously for the excellent tour guide, but also know more that’s on the surface (if You know what I mean). Valerio seems like have a perfect blend of general knowledge and underground knowledge as well, because I was asking his questions constantly and he seems to be on top of the game. (Just example would be the water battles in the Colosseum), on top of that he is an Architect, so he was well equipped with the knowledge of arch building in Ancient Rome and use this additional perk to explain why this massive structures hold up until today.
4. Guides MUST read the crowd. What I mean by that – is they should be able to read the people face expressions that they understand material, keep connections with them, make proper brakes, take them to shades when possible.
So this is my quick list of excellent tour guides, just my personal opinion.

So the tour itself lasts about 3 hours, You’ll have to cross the street with crazy car drivers, like Valerio Jokes with gods help we’re crossing the streets in Italy 😊.

Then enjoy the tour with Your guide which will be around an hour, You’ll be taken to first floor first, then to the top floor, if You have problems with stairs, which will be some, do not be shy and ask for elevators.
On the top floor enjoy the views, inside and outside.

Once You done with the tour in Flavian Amphitheater (real name of the Colosseum), sorry for the spoil, but then You’re going into Ancient Rome which includes Roman Forum, Palatine Hill and surroundings.

On the way there will be restroom break and water break, remember to keep Your water filled, Romans use fountains for water, to refill and the water is perfectly fine (I say put part of Rome into Your blood), but if You have problem with that, there will be vending machine, which servers Coke and Bottled water so no problem here as well.

Once You enjoyed the Ancient Rome, You’ll end the tour next to Julius Caesar altar. Do not forget to give Your audio box back to the tour guide. I managed to forget anyway was so exited so I ran to see Ancient Rome myself, but it’s not a problem to return, I called CitiWondes and they told me not to worry, just gave them name of the hotel that I stayed at and they’ll pick it up from receptionist.

Also do not forget to tip to the excellent tour guide if You feel, couple of Euros is fine, but make sure You have the change, unlike me who could not break 50 euro on the spot.

I guess that’s it. I hope it’ll help You to navigate the complex Rome adventure. Below I’m attaching official mail from City Wonders regarding the tour, so You have full info as of June 2019.

We took the 10 am tour. It was very chaotic at the meeting point .
We had to queue to get in although the trip was advertised as “skip the line”.
The Guide took us around the colosseum at break neck speed. It was already crowded and we were in and out in 30 minutes. Having read the guide book later there was a lot of information we hadn’t been told.
The Guide was better as we got to the forum and palatine hill (although we weren’t shown Caesars pyre ). Luckily we had gone around the forum the day before on our own so already knew a bit about some of the architecture.
I think we were very unlucky with our guide.

After an amazing morning tour of the Vatican with City Wonders, we had high hopes for our afternoon tour of the Colosseum, Forum and Palantine Hill. Unfortunately, these expectations were not met.

We met our guide (I think her name was Martha) at 2pm. She was pleasant and friendly, and introduced herself with a warm handshake and a big smile. A good start! However it went slightly downhill from there.

She took the group to one side and explained that she would show us round the Colosseum first, then we would head over to the Forum and Palantine Hill, where she would leave us at 4pm, the tour lasting 2 hours. There were a few looks of confusion around the group as the tour was advertised as being 3 hours, this was what we were expecting and what we had paid for. Someone did attempt to challenge her on this, but she answered with 'Yes, it's 3 hours, till 4pm. 2, 3, 4, 5. Oh no 5pm. It lasts 2 hours. Oh, I don't know.' So the good start quickly turned to confusion and disappointment.

After a bit of information about the building of the Colosseum, all done outside, we then walked round to an entrance, where Martha attempted to get us in. However, she was turned away and told to walk back to the other line for the groups. On the way back round, she said that she was normally allowed in that entrance so she didn't know why we were being told to go to the other one, however she made no attempt to challenge the person who turned her away. We then had to join the back of the 'Group entrance' line where we waited for a good 15 minutes to get through security. So much for 'skip the line'!

Once we were inside, we were given some more basic information on the gladiators and architecture. However, this was very basic and it felt that she was reciting from a book. There was no passion or enthusiasm and she just kept telling us to use our imagination. This is fair enough as the Colosseum today looks significantly different to what it did back then, but she didn't really motivate us to use our imagination, other than show us a few pictures. A lot of the questions she was asked were met with a reply of 'I don't know' or she would not understand and would just repeat facts she had given earlier.

A good chunk of the tour was Martha leaving us to look around ourselves. I can understand giving us a few minutes to take pictures but it felt that we had to learn a lot for ourselves. She gave us 15 minutes to look round the museum section, and I saw other tour groups being led to different points in the museum where they would be given information on the displays, this did not happen with us.

There were many opportunities during the tour for Martha to cram as much interesting information in as possible (this is what I expect from a guided tour anyway), for example, the wait in the queue, the Museum section, the walk to the Forum. However, she seemed to be more interested during this time in entertaining a child who was part of the group, talking about their holiday etc. Not what we paid to hear about! This was particularly frustrating when we overheard other guides (with both City Wonders and other companies) using every opportunity to provide as much information as they could.

She even said further on into the tour how it was her 4th tour of the day and how the guides had to say the same stuff several times a day. It sounded like she was complaining about doing her job and did not help my suspicions that she just couldn't really be bothered at this point in the day.

When we arrived at the Forum at around 3.30, she pointed at a couple of arches, gave us their names, but didn't tell us the significance of them. She then showed us where the Forum once stood, then showed us another picture. We walked a bit further through to where the toilets were situated and then stopped so people could use the bathroom. By this time it was about 3.45pm so I thought maybe the tour would go on till 5 as advertised, if we were stopping for a bathroom break. However, after waiting for 10 minutes for people to use the bathroom, she then collected the radios back, confirming it was the end of the tour.

I left feeling disappointed and a bit short-changed. Seeing the Colosseum has been on mine and my partner's bucket list for some years, so after seeing so many brilliant reviews, I thought I couldn't go wrong in booking this tour. So for us to get a 2 hour tour which was advertised as a 3 hour tour, then to only have spend about 20 minutes of that tour actually being given information, was incredibly disappointing. It was still amazing to visit and see the Colosseum, Forum and Palantine Hill, but they were not done justice by a lacklustre tour guide, who whilst friendly enough, gave minimal facts and just seemed a bit fed up.

Reading the other reviews, it seems that this tour can be amazing, it just depends who you get as your guide which I certainly feel shouldn't be the case.

Really bad experience. My wife and I left the tour early. The guide didn't speak very good Enlgish and also the group was larger than the "maximum" group size of 25 people that they state on the website. It was really busy at the Colosseum and so we spent a large amount of time keeping everyone together and doing head counts. For this site you definitely do not need a guide.

We did several City Wonders tours all over Italy on our 11 day trip. Some of them were amazing and some were a little flat. The Colosseum and Ancient Rome tour was one of the flat ones, It takes so long to get into the colosseum, i totally get the need for that kind of security, but it should be factored into the tour length. The tour itself was essentially a walk around the second floor and back out of the area and across the way to the Ancient Rome part of the tour. My family and I really wanted to see the floor, and all of the amazing work it took to get the gladiators and animals to the floor. Lastly, we didn’t even have. A moment to go to the gift shop. I really wanted to.

Although 'skip the line', we went through a considerable line to reach security checkpoint at the entrance of the Colosseum, at which point I was refused entry as I was carrying a "trolley" type backpack ( a backpack with wheels to carry as hand luggage on airplanes). Despite not much bigger than regular backpacks and despite the fact that I was carrying it on my back and not having it wheeled around. There is no baggage room at the venue, I was simply denied entry and left to my own devices by the tour guide, while security was complaining why had the tour guide named Renata, not informed me before of the issue. Also no information about this restriction on the company's tour info. So I had to exist the Colosseum and I started door-knocking in the area and after two refusals, the third place, a Trattoria, accepted to store my backpack so that I could rejoin the tour. Having mixed a full hour and then struggling to find by group in the immensity of the Colosseum for another hour, I did not get much from the tour. I was simply happy that I could get the view of the interior and some photos, and be reunited with my wife who had stayed with the group. To make up for the lost time, we decided to stay behind and not exit the Colosseum with the group, not realising that we'll be missing on the "Ancient Rome" part of the tour. Again I am disappointed with the tour guide as she simply took our headsets and said good bye without informing us that we'll be missing on the last part of the tour. It has been a poorly organised and chaotic half-tour for us.

Perfect guide for our tour you realy do need to be in a small group. We turned up for our tour to be asked for our passports for Id. We said we had no passports on us they were at the hotel, we didn't realise we needed picture Id. We had to travel well over an hour back to our hotel for our passports. When we returned we weren't even asked for them, so obviously didn't need them, no one else was asked either. We were charged another 60 Euro on top of the 120 Euro already paid, to fit us in a later tour because of the passports ( that weren't checked !).This wasn't the Colosseum, it was the company used by Trip advisor. There were a few unhappy people that day.

The tour started a bit away from the colosseum and we had some good details about the surrounded Roman forums. The colosseum itself is simply amazing and a must see!

The night tour is defiantly the better option as there were only a small hand full of other groups rather than the 30,000+ people who visit each day so you had time & space to enjoy & marvel at the wonders & magnitude of the Colosseum.

Also when we visited it’s been 30+ degrees during the day and I can’t imagine how uncomfortably hot this would of made the tour in and out of the colosseum, the night tour is defiantly the way to go!

Simply amazing!!

Booked the 10 o’clock 3hr walking tour - Alessandro was our guide - very good English very friendly and knowledgeable. Would recommend this tour - take your own water,hat and parasol.
Thoroughly enjoyed the 3 hrs and the knowledge of our tour guide.
The weather was very hot even although it was September.
The only down in this review is the constant and I mean constant street sellers - as you queue to register and wait to start the tour they must have asked us about 20-30 times water, parasol, selfie stick ?!?!?!
It’s not just here but all over the major tourist destinations- when you are with children it’s quite annoying.

Excellent tour starting off with a Colosseum tour that skipped the line and took in various levels of the arena, then to the Palatine Hill with great access to hard to see parts of the Roman Imperial palace and then freedom to explore the Forum. As someone who reads a lot of books on ancient Roman history it was great to have a guide who was highly knowledgeable of all the details and able to pass that information over in a easy way. She was also very friendly and helpful with photos etc for all different types of guest (I was on my own).

I have visited the Colosseum three time now, our recent visit we were offered the tour to the fifth level inside the Colosseum, if you are not able to see the bottom level take advantage of seeing the top level. The view is pretty cool at a higher level. This was a private tour since the gates do have to be open to enter the stairway.

I forgot the name of the tour company but they were British guys offering the tour and the tourist guide was Italian in the colosseum however in the palatine hills the guy who toured us was not a local and it was a bit disappointing as we were joined together with the different tours when we reached palatine hills. We were like hoards of tourist and the experience was not that great.the lady holding a Japanese umbrella was really a good historian . I loved her choice of words in describing the ancient history. If you see her in the coliseum, make sure it’s her who is the tour guide.

Three of us took the Colosseum & Ancient Rome Small Group Tour with Forum & Palatine Hill. Wish I could say I enjoyed all the sights, but we left the tour at the colosseaum because we were so disappointed with the experience. I'm not one to complain normally, but what was meant to be an informative and exciting experience was more like listening to someone talk on their phone. Guilia spent more time talking about the process of getting into the sight than providing information about the site. We handed in our headsets and went back to the start to take the colosseaum in on our own and were disspointed to hear more exciting and informative tours being given by other companies. Maybe we just got a bad guide, but it was a massive let down.

We went on this tour today. This was the Colosseum Group Tour, promoted as "skip the line". We had originally booked the tour that included underground access, but this was cancelled by City Wonders a few days before our arrival, but the time was kept the same. There was no explanation as to why it was that the underground tour was cancelled.
The tour started with a 45 minute wait in line. I think this was due to the excessive crowds on Easter Monday; however we were on one of the earliest tours. Perhaps by knowing that this was a very busy day, less tours should have been booked? This was a rough start for our youngest child. Our guide was very kind, however she was a bit difficult to understand, and she was not very enthusiastic. Although the sights were amazing, we were all glad when it was over. This place (Colosseum, Forum, Palatine Hill) has so many amazing stories to be told, but it was never captivating in any way. Overall we are glad we went, but for the price, it wasn't the experience we were expecting.

Nov 21: 10am Tour

Our tour guide Assunta was awesome ( see our photos) !!! Very knowledgeable. She was so detailed and very pleasant with how she tells us the story of all the tour sites. I liked it when she answered my questions & others enthusiastically. It was not a boring tour' lol. This is an awesome tour! I would pick "City Wonders" and Assunta as our tour guide next time when i come back with friends or family.

This was my second time in Rome and will come here again (was here 2016 w/ another tour co.). We met up in the hill above the Metro Blue Line station. We had to look for the meeting place. Make sure if you are going to take the bus, that you will end up the Metro Blue Line because we took the wrong bus ( Bus 46 from our hotel) and we stopped at Piazza Venezia area and we had to walk about 30 minutes to the Colosseo. If you have ample time, the walk would be great as you get to see the Palatine Hill on the street side along "Via dei Fori Imperialli". We did not mind the walk because we had some time to spare.

Once you see the Colosseo and because you are supposed to meet with "City Wonders" tourguide ( dont go to the entrance of the Colosseo), you must go up the stairs from the Metro Blue Line "Colosseo" station and look for the center part where there is a mini-circular elevated ground area-- not along the fence. If you pre-booked ( which is better to pre-booked), look for the agency tour name and usually the tour guides have their names on little flags which they wave around for you to see them. They wont look for you. You have to look for them. You should not be paying any cash to any of these tour guides (tips ok). You will see people on having "City Tours banners/ ads" on motorbikes; be careful with these people.. They are there to get your money once you talk to them, they wont let you go and if you dont deal with them you get insulted. Be smart and be careful who you deal with. Bring water to drink & snack or sandwich and dont bring too much stuff in your backpack; leave space for souvenirs:)
Overall I am very satisfied with City Wonders 5 Star! although 3 hour, it was just right because we have time to walk around the area of the Colosseo.

*Tip: Pre-book a "City Tour Sight Seeing Hop On/Off Bus" and check if the bus stops it are close to your hotel and just walk to your hotel. We did! The hotel we took was close to the Vatican and we had taken a Hop On/Off Bus and walked towards Castle Sant' Angelo and also saw the Vatican at night then to our hotel all within 30 minutes walking distance. Get very comfy sneakers w/ arch so you wont have sore feet.

Sadly I spent £200 on this tour, expecting it to be worth it as the highlight of our trip to Rome - how wrong was I! Do not take your kids (mine are 8 and 11) on this tour, but instead get some really fun details about the lives of gladiators and who worked here. If you take this tour, you risk getting someone like our tour guide who talked mainly about the stone work for nearly three hours. Instead of inspiring and entertaining, we struggled to bribe the kids to stick with it. Very disappointed. And no refund possible apparently.

On March 16th I booked the Skip the Line: Ancient Rome and Colosseum Half Day Walking Tour for myself and husband. Today, 2 months after booking and 2 weeks from the tour date scheduled, I got a call saying my tour was cancelled. They gave me options to change my date (which didn't end up working for our travel schedule), downgrade to a different tour with a partial refund, or cancel altogether. I really hope this isn't a sign of things to come because we have SEVERAL other tours scheduled through them while in Italy because I trusted all the good reviews on here and Viator. Even thinking that all my time researching and planning could end up wasted makes me shudder. It's disappointing that there was nothing more they could work out for us considering how much money we currently have tied up in booked tours through them. Needless to say, this review is titled "so far, not so good" . I guess the tours could be great, if they don't cancel them on you. Just have a back up plan if you book with them.

We had a well organized and interesting tour of the Colosseum, Roman Forum, & Palatine Hill. The guide was knowledgable and friendly and handled our moderately size crowd (which included some young children very well).

I think you have to go with a guide to get the most out
Of a visit to the colosseum. Our guide was very knowledgeable and spoke English really well.
The only negative were the uncomfortable earphones.

Our guide was good. He was enthusiastic, knowledgeable about the Colosseum and the Forum, and maybe could've been a little more "up with the times" on some aspects of his history (Domitian's not really considered a "bad" emperor anymore) but overall we were very satisfied.

The real problem: you will not actually "Skip the Line" with this tour. You don't wait in line to buy tickets — but you still have to wait in the same security lines for the Colosseum and Roman Forum as everyone else. And the security lines are really long. We had a 9:30am tour and we spent probably 90 minutes of the three-hour tour waiting in line.

TLDR: skip this tour and get a Roma card if you don't want to wait in the ticket line.

We had to wait during the start of the tour which I dont mind, and wait a bit more to enter the colosseum. Once we entered, the guide mentioned that we only have 1 hour (this was not mentioned in the tour package description) to tour the Colosseum! It wasn't enough as firstly, to get an audio guide, we'd have to lined up to buy them in which we obviously dont have enough time for that. Secondly, the colosseum is filled with collections of histories on the top floor where even with fast reading, took me at least 20 mins to read them. Thirdly, the Colosseum is huge and to actually be immersed with the architecture and appreciate it within another 30 mins was definitely not enough! Another 10 mins was used to find our way out to gather for Roman Forum fast access. Note that if you missed the gathering time even by a few mins, you'd be left behind with no other way to access to Roman Forum as the entry was only by using the guide group ticket. In Roman Forum, we were left to explore to our heart content.

It's great to skip the line but I was really disappointed with the amount of time allowed to roam in Colloseum. I'd suggest that City Wonder would actually provide the same fast access to get audio guide which would have been a great help to those interested and at least lengthen the touring time to one and a half hours or provide a separate ticket to enter the Roman Forum at our own time after we're done with the Colosseum.

I was there for holiday from South East Asia and was really looking forward for my visit to Colosseum but was utterly devastated with the tour timing.

Our "half day walking tour " with "professional guide and headsets to hear your guide clearly" was mis-sold. We were walked into the Colosseum, set loose for 50 minutes to look around on our own, then we were walked to the forum where, again, we were set free to explore on our own, at which point the guide then departed. We were in his company for a total of half an hour max, so although he was very pleasant and obviously very knowledgeable, (he gave us a couple of minutes' information outside both monuments), we had no benefit of his expertise as we looked around. No headsets, no tour, just a skip the line ticket and his help to cross the road outside the Colosseum.

We took this tour in Sept. it wasn’t that hot , but warm in the sun . There is a lot of walking and stairs - so be prepared . Very little smooth pathways . Our guide was good , but maybe talked a little too much and she wore her microphone around her neck and couldn’t hear her half the time ! She did stop a few times and tried to get in the shade . There was a bathroom stop that was good . However the tour says you can’t take anything with you , so we took nothing . The guide said she hoped I brought water !! There were people with bags etc ! Also , it said your knees and shoulders had to be covered for The Pantheon - our guide was wearing shorts !! So scrap that- wear and take what you want !

We took a cab to the meeting place - Largo Gaetana Agnesi - to ensure we'll be on time. We signed up for the 10:00 tour. Our guide was Rosanna. She had a good command of the English language and we had no problem understanding her. There were 16 in our group including 3 children. We were slightly delayed during our entry to to Colosseum as our admission papers were for only 15 persons. Rosanna adeptly moved us to the side and talked about how the Colosseum came to be. After a delay of 10 minutes, everything was settled and we moved forward. Rosanna provided us historical tidbits of the areas (Colosseum, Roman Forum, Palatine Hill) and patiently answered our questions. One comment I have for the tour operator - the headsets provided were hard on the ears. The headsets we got at the Vatican Skip the Line tour were much better as they had rubber inserts.
Overall - a very good tour. Grazie mille Rosanna!
Was very impressed with this tour. Tour operator was very knowledgeable. She knew her history and made the tour flow well.

This was only my second experience paying for a guided tour, and I can honestly say that this is well worth it for MOST (not all) people. Below are some of the stand-out details from my family's experience...

- Our guide Sylvia was a trained archaeologist, and extremely interactive with us
- The pacing and periodic rest stops were well spaced out
- Tons of great educational points about Roman life back in the day, architectural details of the colosseum, the pine trees, the Romulus/Remus founding legend, and the transition of Rome from Republic to empire to holy Roman empire (THERE WAS A TON)

If you're a parent planning for preteens/teens (like me), I'd recommend doing this. Your kids may give a little push back from all the walking and the heat, but it is worth it afterwards.

Had a great 3.5 hour tour with Sylvia, she was lovely, engaging and an archaeologist!! Best experience we had in Rome was on this tour so don't hesitate to book. Bring water, expect to do a bit of walking although they take it at a lovely pace and always look for shade. Can't recommend this tour highly enough!

We loved this tour and especially our guide, Silvia. She was everything a tour guide should be: funny, attentive, informative and passionate. It was so refreshing to see someone so enthused about their job. You could just see how proud she was to be an archeologist and her love and enthusiasm for Rome's incredible historical significance was infectious. The tour was well structured and easy to find/check-in and Silvia did her best to get us in he shade regularly to help alleviate the unforgiving heat on the day.
I would happily book with City Wondera again and recommend to friends and family. Silvia also gave us some amazing recommendations at the end for places to eat great food as well as an excellent rooftop bar to grab a few drinks at later on that we definitely wouldn't have found otherwise.

Grazie, Silvia - you made us love Rome nearly as much as you do! Ciao

This would’ve been a great tour if he stopped talking so much!!!! The one that speaks English! I’m ready to go damn he y’all too much! I’m saying we spent most of the time listening to him talk! I wanted to take pics and stuff! If you don’t wanna listen to him talk endlessly DONT TAKE THIS TOUR! 😩😩

Myself & my partner were initially reluctant to do a guided group tour but are so glad we did! We had the lovely Serefina as our guide and a group of 10 on the day. Serefina was an excellent guide with so much knowledge & passion for Rome which made the tour enjoyable & run smoothly. Skip the queue was fantastic. Would 100% recommend. Also make sure to do the early morning tour as the Colosseum just gets more and more crowded throughout the day!

We were originally signed up for an underground tour. It was cancelled at the last minute and this tour was substituted. That disappointment aside, this was a good tour. I wish these tours would include more walking and talking, and less standing and talking. However, overall it was an awesome experience.

We booked the 10am tour and the crowds were already piling up. We had to wait a few minutes before entering - so keep in mind when booking. The earlier the better. Our tour guide, Rosy, was awesome. She led our small group of 15 through the entrance pointing out special details and historical facts. We started with the Colosseum and the made our way to the Forum to see all of the ancient surroundings. July in Rome is hot, so make sure to bring a bottle water if you are traveling in the summer months. The tour was great but Rosy made it even better. Throughout our tour we climbed stairs and maneuvered through crowds in warm temperatures and Rosy didn't even flinch. She kept on with all of the facts and stories of ancient times. I thought I knew a good deal about ancient Rome, but learned so much more. In total this was a three hour tour and we were able to skip the long lines that wrapped around the Colosseum to get in. This is all outdoors with little shelter, so bring your hat or sunglasses too! Hopefully you will be lucky enough to have Rosy lead you on your tour through the Colosseum! She made this a highlight of our stay in Rome!

Definitely worth the purchase! The normal line outside is insane. Looked to be at least 1 hr to get in through security.

Tour guide:
Sara G was our wonderful guide today. She was super friendly and upbeat. We learned so many new things from her. Bring money for gratuity.

Start Time:
Arrive 10-15 mins prior to tour in front of the colosseum.
Check in with the blue shirt person holding the tablet.
From there you’ll be directed to tour guide.
Tour guide will give you a sticker for your shirt and a headset with headphones.
The headphones were terrific for the tour. It gets somewhat loud inside but the headphones allow you to be able to hear your guide.

Attire:
Wear tennis shoes! Tons of walking. There are stairs involved as well.
Wear a hat & wear sunblock.
Water- you can bring a bottle of water or buy one from one of the numerous peddlers outside. 2 bottles = 3 euros.

City wonder was not super organized in getting us together but once we got started with our guide everything was great. Our guide was super knowledgeable and flexible and shared information about Ancient Rome and the Colosseum and surrounding area‘s. It was amazing to learn about the history of the Colosseum, Palatine hill, and the Roman forum. We had two families with kids ranging from age 4 to 16 and we all had something to find interesting.

This is so damn ridiculous. I paid for three tickets £148. My mom and I arrived at the meeting point at 2.45pm, and I informed the staff that my dad was still on the way. I was being brushed off by their bitchy attitude multiple times by two staff wearing the blue polo tees. When my dad arrived at 2.58pm they didn’t allow him to join the tour as the tour group couldn’t “accommodate” him. Is this a joke? I demand a refund for the terrible service and for not allowing my dad to go on the tour that we ALREADY paid for.

We were lucky to have such nice weather on the day of tour (partly cloudy, temp in the low 60 degree F). Our guide was Cecilia who has tremendous knowledge and innate ability to make us feel immerse in the ancient time as it was over 2000 years ago at the site. She told us the significant of each point of interest then when move on to the next one, she summarized them again then point us back to that point so we can better understand the historic sites. This tour requires lot of walking and climbing stairs to truly appreciate this wonder so do it when you are healthy and prepare.
If you want to avoid the crowds join a later afternoon tour! Our informed guide made the visit come alive with stories of political shenanigans and ancient Roman gossip and gore.

We booked our tour in advance and it was well worth it. When you arrive there are so many people trying to sell you tickets and tours, it’s overwhelming. And with the crowd you have to be mindful of pick pocketing. We were able to just walk through and meet up with our guide. He was very knowledgeable and it certainly made it easier to get through the crowd. We also stopped for bathroom break. Well
Worth it !

Strictly speaking we didn’t book this but I was given it as a gift for my (getting on in other people’s eyes) birthday. If we had done this off our own backs we would have queued for access, walked around swiftly and probably not have even realised that the forum and palatine hill area even existed. Katia our guide came across as very knowledgable about the whole area and we found this very informative and we thoroughly enjoyed the whole experience. It’s a shame we couldn’t have had good weather booked but we soldiered on in the threatening storm. Anyone visiting Rome for the first time needs to do this tour.

My husband and I were searching for a tour of the Colosseum, it was so overwhelming with so many to choose from. We struck gold finding this one with City Wonders. With headphones to hear the guide you won’t miss a thing. Our guide Ema was fantastic, he’s an archeologist and is very passionate about his city. We learnt so many fun and interesting facts on this tour and have a whole new respect for the history of this amazing city.

We were more than a little hesitant to join anything that had people recruiting customers as we approached, but in the end we were so very glad to have taken this tour. We started at the Colosseum, which included access to parts of the building that weren't otherwise accessible. Our guide was amazingly knowledgeable and her enthusiasm was clear. The tour then continued to the Palantine Hill and the Forum, and we had the great pleasure of having David as our guide. With David, it was not so much a tour as a comedy show with the most amazing historical props as backdrop. He is very knowledgeable, and very very funny. Find out what tour(s) David is giving, and take those.
We loved this tour. Our guide, Rosanna, was a lot better than our Vatican guide he day before & the sights were breathtaking. What an amazing society the Romans created 2,000 years ago
This walking tour was excellent. Our guide Michela shared many details along the tour. It was a chilly day but very enjoyable. Be prepared to walk.

This was not a skip the line experience. We waited over 90 minutes to get in and then only had 45 minutes before being rushed off to the forum. Do not pay for this experience as there is no value - the regular ticket line was much faster.

The tour was ok, it only lasted 2 hours, not half day. The guide had knowledge of the Colosseum, but didn’t give hardly any info on the Roman Forum or Palatine Hill, we just went up to the highest overlook and he pointed a few things out. It was hot so most people thought this was just fine. He didn’t leave a lot of time for pictures at the Colosseum.

This is an absolute must for visitors to Rome. I’ve taken two CityWonders tours so far, and they are worth every penny. Nicola was our guide to the Colosseum, Roman Forum and Palatine Hill. He was friendly, knowledgeable and fun. Be prepared for stairs and hills. The two historic sites have scanners like the airport, so travel light and don’t take anything that might appear suspicious. They have amazing things to protect!

Your experience will depend entirely on whether you get a good guide. I did the 3pm tour on 13 sept with Laura. I felt that she was not engaging enough and her explanations were kind of dry. The tour could have been more lively.

Our guide Gio was amazing, really knew her stuff. Explained things clearly with good humor and she really looked after us well. She really brought the Colosseum to life. Would highly recommend this tour.

I thoroughly enjoyed this tour. Our guide Marco was extremely enthusiastic and knowledgeable and took great care of the group. The Colosseum is understandably very crowded but he made the best use of the time we had to see and learn as much as possible and also tried to personalise the tour as much as possible. I recommend the first tour of the day if possible.

There are no really negatives to this.

You have a knowledgable guide who takes you on a journey through history and ensures you get to understand the things you are seeing and puts them into context.

You can come back solo and soak it all in further on another day of visit. But this does give you a great grounding (and quick access).

The earpiece means you don’t have to follow like a flock of sheep but can keep distance and have private time.

My advice is to do this. But lotion up as it’s hot and take water. There are lots of places to top up the bottle on the tour and keep hydrated.

This was my favorite tour we did throughout Italy, by far! The skip the line is worth the price by itself, as the lines are quite long during peak months. Adding in a great tour guide who provides endless history and fun facts throughout the tour. I enjoy history and was truly amazed to hear details about the construction, building materials, why it looks as it does today and so much more! Worth every penny, definitely a must do in Roma!

Definitely worth it! We got to skip the line, and go straight in to security. The process was brief and easy. Once inside, our guide spoke about the different meanings and activities that went on in the colosseum. If you are short on time, this tour is definitely worth it!

We really enjoyed this tour, city wonders were well organised and our guide Christina was both very knowledgeable and understanding of the needs of the group. She explained the many interesting aspects making sure everyone understood. She made an outstanding visit extra special

Completed a tour today, so first things..it’s hot, there are a lot of steps....we lost a few people at the start because of the climb...there is little shade so be prepared.....however it was fabulous...educational, inspiring , informative....we got a 2000 year history lesson today and that was amazing.

For no other reason you should book the tour in order to avoid the long and chaotic line to get into the colosseum. That being said our guide Ahmed was great and provided great historical insight. I think without that background and description it would be hard to imagine or get a lot out of viewing the ruins of the colosseum, forum, and palatine hill. Ahmed was also extremely patient, allowing plenty of time for pictures, water breaks, and restrooms. There is no avoiding the masses at these sights, but the tour made it much more enjoyable.
Our tour guide Alessandro was amazing!!!! So knowledgeable and interesting. Lots of walking and very exhausting but well worth it. Loved this tour!

More than half of our group tapped out about half way, which turned the group into a private tour of about 7 people. Fabio was amazing and did an excellent job sharing so much history. Be prepared for some serious walking, but Fabio makes it so entertaining and interactive. Be weary of all the scammers in the meeting area (one of them pretty much stole 5 euros from us).

We had a great experience the group was 25 people, the guide made sure everybody was in the group listening and answering question all the time. His explanation were very good and the visit to the Colosseum was just as we had expcted and maybe even better. Then he took us walking to the old city with its magnificent ruins and explain the history behind it. At the end he even gave us tips on what not to miss and places to eat. The tour is great the views of the Colosseum just great.

Brilliant tour of the Colosseum, Forum and Palatine Hill with Halina. We did the 3pm tour time which finished around 6pm. It was done perfectly with the colosseum first then onto Palatine Hill and finally the Forum. She was great at giving interesting pieces of history along with plenty of time to explore by ourselves.

The bulk of the tour is in the colosseum which was the best way to do it. When the tour finishes you are left in the Forum and so if you want to explore a little more of the Forum yourself it's very easy to do so.

We paid $142.48 for two to skip the line Colosseum and walking tour of Rome. The maximum amount of people in our tour should not exceed 18 yet we had 22. We also found that the Colosseum offers FREE admission on Sundays therefore our “skip the line” pass was useless. We stood in line for hours waiting to get into Colosseum. By the time we were granted access the tour was over and we did not see anything else as our guide said sorry times up. I have requested a refund from this company but have not had a response from them.

The tour was awesome! Rome is busier than you can imagine, and there are people everywhere. Cecilia from City Wonders was our guide, and she did an outstanding job. She knew all of the history like the back of her hand, and she made sure that we saw everything that we should see. I though that the Colosseum was going to be the highlight of the tour, but I was mistaken, The Forum was amazing, and Cecilia knew so many intricate details about the history of the area. I would definitely recommend this tour to anyone who has half a day to spend. Make sure that you go early (I took the 8:30A tour), and make sure that you can walk 2+ miles in 3 hours. if I could give a 6 star rating, I would.

I had tried to book a visit to the Colosseum on the official site – and failed. I am glad that I did; on this occasion, fortune favoured the incompetent. A friend who had recently visited Rome had the same experience but had found and strongly recommended the 'Skip the Line Tour'. I booked it for my family of adults and young people. One of my best Roman decisions.

Our guided group was about 30 persons – all English speaking – led by our Guide, Dave, who was knowledgeable and enthusiastic. The tour lasted about 3 hours, but towards the end, in the Forum, it was easy to leave early or stay as long as you wished after the official finish. I thought I knew a lot about history of the Colosseum, but Dave gave us far far more insight and brought it to life.

I have forgotten the cost but think it was about £10 per head more than ‘doing it ourselves’. It was worth every extra Euro. Walking past long hot queues - we had a child with us - was an enormous relief, as was being taken around the site in a logical order since it is confusing to say the least. A knowledgeable guide is much more than just icing on the cake. This tour is very highly recommended.

HINTS:

1. You cannot always choose when you go to Rome, so it may not be possible to choose when to go to the Colosseum. Whenever you decide to visit, go as early in the day as you can. In high summer, I would not go at all; the sun and heat must be close to intolerable.

2. Take bottles of water.

3. There is lot of walking, mostly on uneven pavements, and some very steep flights of steps. My personal view – although others may disagree - is that the tour is not suitable for children under 8, nor for anyone who is infirm. That said, you can leave the tour when you have had enough.

4. The site is crowded so do watch your pockets and your valuables.

First the computer book us the wrong date. Second, when we call explaining the situation using the TripAdvisor app and viator book is on the wrong date, the woman from Italy city wonder yours could have care less. They wanted a 15 euro reticketing fee and would not accommodate anything. We said we have the flight that morning and they do not care. They could not find us two spots the day earlier so I have to go by myself and pay another 15 euro reticketting fee on top of the 108 euro we paid for our tickets. They would not accommodate my mother so she has to stay behind. She said there is no more spot but would issue a credit for us 6 months. We would not be in Rome in the next 6 mths!!! We were just there!! The guide is much worst since she lost 2 people on the tour since she didn’t care so much about the people she took on tour. I would skip this TripAdvisor advertisement of this company and do it yourself.

We were so disappointed with the visit today. Our guide Paolo Emilio had so little to offer on such a broad and diverse topic and even when we tried to prompt him with questions to elicit more information/ try to make the most of what was a pretty deathly experience he had very little to offer besides the standard printouts of computer generated images of what things might have looked like at the time - and even then struggled with these. Of course it did not help as we passed other tour groups and observed how actively engaged their guides were with their groups.

We signed up for the "Skip the Line" Half-day Walking Tour of Ancient Rome and the Colosseum with the upgrade to the extra behind the scenes to the underground and upper terrace. My documents included directions to find the start of the tour which were we written and easily followed. Once we arrived it was down hill from there. The " Skip the Line", is actually an enter through a group tour line. It wasn't crowded when we got there so it moved fairly quickly but it definitely was not "skipping" any line as the tour guide, "Jebar" got our tickets for entry.

Once we entered we were required to wait at least 30 minutes while we waited for the "Special Guide" to unlock the gate for the Underground. While waiting, "Jebar" kept repeating himself, explaining his 40 plus years as a guild and how he was an expert on the Colosseum. He did provide some information I did not know but mostly it was information anyone could glean from Wikipedia. Once the "Special Guide" arrived we got to walk on the makeshift wood, stage floor while the "Special Guide" repeated what "Jebar" was saying during our wait. The underground was disappointing as we walked under the stage we had been standing on, stopped in a walkway to look at several caverns that they said the animals were stored in. We saw and archway that led to the gladiator training facility but nothing about gladiator holding areas or rooms. There was a replica of the lift that animals may have been used to enter the Colosseum floor by with an explanation of the device although it was not operated or demonstrated to us.

We moved to the mid-level of the Colosseum that every tourist and guided tour goes to for viewing for more explanation with more repeat of previous information. We were forced to wait for our guide while he waited in the long elevator line so two folks could take the elevator up, apparently no "skip the elevator line" included. it was crowded and the "special photo op" spot our guide wanted us to use was too crowed so we moved on to a lessor spot.

I pointed to the upper terrace and asked "Jebar" when we were going to the upper terrace? His response was that is a different tour that only the Colosseum provided with "Special Guides". I told him my documents said the upper terrace was included and he said it was not.

We spent over 2 hours at the Colosseum so we had very little time for the Forum and Palatine Hill. That part of the tour was rushed with only a few highlights pointed out. "Jebar" said the Forum and Palatine hill would take a tour of it's own to cover and the Colosseum was the main focus of this tour.

I read a lot about places I'm traveling so perhaps I'm better informed. I found very little the guides said to be new information. The access to the upper terrace was misrepresented and the underground was walk into a hallway under the stage to hear a guide speak, very little of the underground was accessed or viewed that anyone without the "upgraded package" could see. Standing on the mid-level where all tourist have access, you can stand and watch other groups stand in the underground hallway, except for the guides talk, you see what they see.

This was a terrible tour. I took this tour for my brother who had never been out of the USA and wanted a "special" Rome trip. When our week was done, he kept saying he was most disappointed with this tour. he considered it the worse part of the trip and I agree.

Pick another company or just go on your own and read the informative signs at these ancient sites. City Wonders is a waste of money and time.

This was a amazing tour of the Colosseum and the ancient Rome ... Our tour guide Alba was a super star .. taking us through a magical journey back in time . Not only was she very energetic and bubbly; she was very knowledgeable and kept the whole group of all age group engaged throughout the tour ... we finished the tour with a great understanding and respect from the rich Roman history and culture ... a definitely recommended .. thanks Alba for the wonderful experience

Great tour by tour guide, but unfortunately we were told the pass lasted 2 days which it does but it only gives you entry once, so after we left (due to poor weather), we were not allowed back in which resulted in a waste of money.

The tour guide was knowledgable and enthusiastic. The use of headsets to hear the guide was very helpful. Good length of time spent in each place. Had to queue a little for security, but all in all it was worth the money.

Well organised tour keeping numbers to maximum of 25. Tour guide Laura was very knowledgeable and the headsets saved having to try and hear her shouting above the noise. Fast access to the Colloseum jumping the crowds and great to hear more about the history of the forum and Palantine Hill which you would not get just wandering around yourself. Think this turned out to be one of the cheaper walking tours and was very good value overall.

We had an amazing time with Maria Luisa, she was fantastic, very friendly, and knowledgeable, we learned a lot of things!!!
I really appreciated and recommend this tour!!!!

You would never get or understand the history of the colosseum and the forum without a good guide

My tour went almost 4 hours, I was ready for lunch and a rest after this tour

Excellent guide speaks to you with the help of transmitters and earbuds to hear everything even if you lag behind

Great tour. Do this tour you wont regret it

This was the perfect way to see the Colosseum, Roman Forum and Palatine Hill. for most of our 2 week trip around Italy, my husband and I used a tour book and self-guided tours. However, for this particular part of our trip, I would highly recommend a tour like this. Damian is an archeologist and pointed out so many things during our tour that we would have never known to look at. He was extremely informative and friendly and made sure we learned as much as possible.

Very good tour. I thought that the earpieces would be a gimmick but they were a great idea. The whole place is amazing and better than I imagined. A decent price too. My ONLY criticism was that 2 1/12 might be better (especially when it's cold)! Would use them again...
Lousie Kennedy from City Wonders was very friendly and knowledgeable which made for a fantastic day trip!
The tour was very well organized. Our guide spoke well, told us funny stories from the history of Rome and her own life. 3 hours of excursion passed very fast.

It was so much fun listening to the stories about the Colloseum and Roman Forum - our tour guide Sev was very knowledgeable and enthusiastic and he told us so many things that you can't just look up in Wikipedia. 10/10!

Informative friendly factual tour which gave us a full understanding of the colliseums purpose uses and place in archetectural and world history, with a hint to the modern architectural salvage anreconstruction taking place. three hours taking in also the pallatine hill ruins of the living areas of the emporers and there families, along with a knowledgeable acount of the fascinaring forum area delivered in an understanding and friendly manner by sophina [hope i have spelt this correctly]

Great tour, and the skip the line is a must especially in the busy tourist season. Our guide Giuseppe was very knowledgeable, took the time to explain things to the mixed age group so everyone understood, and did so in a entertaining way so that by the end of the tour you didn't even realize you have been walking all through ancient Rome for a couple hours until it was over.

Terrific guide - Jana - who went to Rome from the States to study art history as a grad student and never left. Obviously has perfect English, intelligent, informed, interesting, made the experience really enjoyable. Skipping the line is essential - the lines are endless. Some communication/advertising issues between TripAdvisor and City Wonders - the tour was 2 hours at the Colosseum and expedited entry WITHOUT GUIDED TOUR to the Forum and Palatine Hill despite the description of a 3 hour tour including all 3. Several people on the tour were upset, partly because it was the most expensive option. The City Wonders supervisor was apologetic and blamed TripAdvisor and noted that they would fix the description but it doesn't appear to have happened yet. No matter (at least for us) - the small group, the terrific guide and passing the hordes standing in line by (hundreds if not thousands - even on a cold February day) was worth it.
Definitely worth the price, especially considering that the lines we avoided were a couple of hours long. Nick, our guide, had quite a few interesting facts and kept us engaged.
Brilliant! Our guide, Dennis was very knowledgable and passionate about Roman history. We were so pleased with the tour. Thank you!
Love every minute of this tour and the tour guide was great. It was a little long but it was worth it

Great tour! Our tour guide Alba was very knowledgeable and engaging! She gave us a lot of great information and showed us many important pieces of history. I would highly recommend this tour. It was very crowded at the colosseum but Alba did a great job navigating and organizing the group!

Our tour guide - She had a Matryohska doll tattoo - was STELLAR. I do not have enough words to recommend this tour. It was funny, smart, so informative... it was an incredible way to kick off our honeymoon. Book now!

MariaGrace was full of interesting information. This tour is a must. The history of how humans entertained themselves, the use of slaves to build this magnificent structure, the distance between wealthy and poor, are just a few of the disturbing and fascinating things we learned. Some things never change. C’mon humanity!

My guide DC is a very knowledgeable guide who is passionate in sharing the history and fun facts of the three places. At every location, we were overwhelmed by the long queues and time after time, we could not be more grateful for booking the skip the line tours. Some tourists came with tickets bought online and were shocked to see to have to queue for a long time to get in. Meanwhile, our group wheezed into every location without much hassle. It is going to be a long walk so come with comfortable shoes. It was winter and I thought it would not be so crowded but I was so wrong. I cannot imagine what the crowds would be like during the peak season.
If you can survive a really long tour, I may recommend this but a lot of walking a and explanations. You may get tired soon after if you are a person likes fast moving.
Rosy was such a wonderful tour guide. We are a family of 6 and everyone enjoyed it. The experience is a must for anyone who really wants to be immersed in the history of Rome.
This trip was the best ever, our guide Sev was amazing, his knowledge of Rome history was impressive; we highly recommend this tour
A very fun and informational tour of the oldest parts of Rome! Our tour guide Marielle was extremely outgoing and knew what she was talking out. If you go, try to go with Marielle.
This tour was very informative and our tour guide Patrick was very friendly and engaging. Highly recommended
Excellent guide very knowledgeable made the tour very interesting. Would recommend this tour. Need to be fit as a lot of walking

Skip the line my eye! We had to hang around for forty minutes until the vip tour started. It took us nearly 1.5hours to gget through the security. Thankfully We had been to the collisium a couple of times before so we're able to ave early and not see the forum and palatine hill. Would we use this service again...No!
Worth every penny. Our guide Valentina D.was clearly spoken with excellent English and gave good tips and information to make our visit enjoyable.

Bought this as a gift for my parents, they went in November 2019.
They loved the gift and the place - lived up to expectations, however at the 10.30am slot i booked there were no queues...and it was more than half prices LESS to buy on the ticket door.
aid it was about £20 each and i paid £69
Not ideal!

Couldn't do much about it at that time!

It is advised to take the skip-the-line tour, though more expensive and may not save 100% of the time. Bring bottle of water. Eat first before visiting because not many restaurants close to. Walk slowly so you can learn and see details. A lot of good spots for camera. Though ruins but let us know the glory history of the places. Also feel miserable to the cruelty at that time.

This was a very good tour that was efficiently run with loads of great information. Everything was well paced with plently of time for photographs and to take in the sites. Our guide was very engaging and really knew her stuff, she spoke clearly and had supporting documents in her folder that really built the picture around the remaining bones.

At the end of the time our guide passed on other information about other things to see and do, places to eat and how to get home. All very much appreciated.

Would highly recommend this tour as you woudl not get this all done on your own.

Damian made the tour a success with his knowledge of the sites.

Our only wish was for a longer time. We’ll have to return and spend a few days at rhe forum.

Maria Lucia was an incredible tour guide and was very engaging. I’m so glad we did this tour, as we would missed so much context just walking around by ourselves. She was able to weave the histories behind the different sites. I would highly encourage doing this tour.

Laura was awesome, she knew her stuff. We had a know it all kid and I was worried he was going to hold up the tour. Laura politely ignored him, lol.

The tour ran very smooth and on time.

Take this tour if you want to maximize your time and experience!

I took this tour on Friday November 29, 2019 at 11am with guide Patrick, The experience was an excellent one! We began my meeting just outside the Metro station and were organized into a group of 25 people. Patrick introduced himself and after a short while we were on our away across the street to a special entrance behind the stage. After passing through security quickly Patrick introduced us to another guide named Kristina who manages the tour inside (Patrick stayed with us). We went from the stage, into the underground, and up through each level accessible (including an area only accessible by guides on the third level). Kristina was amazing and her enthusiasm was clear. We were given set times to wander on our own, use restrooms, see bookstore, etc. Once through, Patrick than walked us through the Forum and eventually to Palatine Hill which was fascinating.

One word of caution - this is a walking tour and within the Colosseum we did climb some very old, steep steps, There was an elevator available to get to most levels but nobody in our group asked to use it. Once at the Forum and Palatine Hill and walked at a leisurely pace but often uphill on semi-steep uneven surfaces. Throughout our tour it did rain a little - most had umbrellas or hoods but plan ahead for this as there is no shelter once you are outside the Colosseum. While I thought the group would break apart with some dropping out well before the end, all stayed together which was amazing and a testament to the great guide we had Patrick,

The Colosseum is one of the seven wonders of the world and I likely won't have the chance to return to Rome to see it again so I was extremely pleased to see if with this tour (and I loved the behind-the-scenes elements and the chance to be on the stage!). I highly recommend this tour for anyone visiting Rome and my November day (except for some sun showers) was otherwise perfect with the 60+ degree (F) weather and low crowds.

This tour absolutely enhanced our visit to these outstanding sites. The guide (Kylie) was incredibly enthusiastic and knowledgeable, couldn’t have asked for a better group leader. Have already recommended this tour to friends since returning home and would urge anyone else visiting to take part.

I mean what can I say that hasn’t been said before. The Colosseum is incredible and it’s a must do no matter if you in Rome for 2 days or a week. And I hate that I can’t remember our tour guys name but he was great. We actually did a few tours with city wonder and they were all great.

Our tour guide, GiGi, was amazing! We couldn’t have asked for anyone better! He was extremely knowledgeable, funny and friendly! Even in the rain, this was the best tour we’ve taken so far! Highly recommend!!!

Our tour was amazing! I am happy to have booked this tour, especially with the skip the line perk. Our guides were super friendly and very knowledgeable about the area. I would highly recommend it to everyone wanting this experience. Thank you City Wonders!

Tour covered the Colosseum, the Forum and provided an overview of the Emperors homes. Be prepared to take in more great information than one can absorb in 2+ hours. The sights were stunning and the information from the guide was A+! We highly recommend this tour while you're in Rome.

The only way to avoid perhaps hours of waiting is by going on a guided tour. Once inside the spectacle is truly amazing. You cannot help but be impressed at the organisation and engineering that went on below ground, the archtectural achievement of the the building itself and the statemt it makes about the grandeur of ancient Rome. One of lifes must see places in the worlds must see city.

This was well worth the money for quick access into the Colosseum. We did still have to wait in a line to get signed in and assigned to a tour guide, but it took no more than 20 minutes. The actual line to get into the Colosseum without a pre-purchased ticket was easily 2 hours! The guide escorted us into the Colosseum and gave us some quick tips on what to see and where to go, but then let us wonder around on our own. She also determined a meeting spot and time after to escort us to the Roman Forum and Palantine Hill, we again were free to explore on our own. Highly recommend.

Our tour started early. No bus pick up, you had to meet just near the front of the colosseum, but it was relatively easy to find. The early start and skip the line was vitally important as hundreds and hundreds of people where already lined up at 7.30 in the morning wanting to buy tickets - the lines looked like a few hours wait in broiling heat. The tour was great - we did the colosseum, Palatine hill, Roman forum etc, and it was terrific. We did expect to go under ground at the colosseum but that just did not happen for some reason. Wear really good walking shoes as you do an awful lot of walking on this extensive tour. Was worth the money.

The guide gave us a seamless and informative description of these remarkable structures, weaving into a coherent account the architecture, history, and culture pertaining to these sites. I highly recommend this tour.

I did this tour which is over 3 hours long! I did enjoy it but please note the following points if you plan to book: (1) it is a LONG tour. Bring water although limited rest room breaks (there are street vendors at the meeting point that you can buy water from if you don’t bring); (2) you must have a decent level of physical fitness as there are parts uphill and at the Colosseum itself, the stairs are extremely steep; (3) I personally don’t think it is worth paying the premium to see the parts of the Colosseum that are normally closed off (I felt it was an anti-climax and it was something I was super excited to see); (4) when you get to the Colosseum itself, your tour joins more tours and a different guide takes you round (although our initial guide stayed with us, he handed over to another guide). I personally didn’t like this. Our tour group initially was a nice size and I felt it was too big once we joined 2 other groups. Also (first world problem I know) but I didn’t like having 2 radios round my neck - one for the tour and a different one for the Colosseum with the different guide); finally (5) I did feel like the process of finding the guide etc was a bit shambolic but perhaps that was to be expected with such a popular tour at one of Rome’s most popular attractions and isn’t a direct criticism of the operator itself (once you found them in their blue polo shirts)

One major plus was that our guide was super knowledgeable and really brought the whole tour to life. He really was a major plus. The pace of the tour was great - I didn’t feel rushed and I didn’t feel bored. Honest opinion: great if you have money to burn but I really don’t think it was worth nearly £100 (and definitely don’t spend the extra to enter the bits below the Colosseum!!!!)

This tour was great because we got to skip the super long line at the colosseum. There was no guided tour but instead we had an hour to explore the colosseum ourselves. We really appreciated that. Same with the Roman forum.
We really enjoyed the tour. Our guide was very knowledgeable and communicated well. The radio earphones were absolutely necessary in the colosseum crowds.

We visited during our honeymoon and opted for a guided tour to learn more about the Colosseum's history.
